paras: The attempted lynching of William Duffy took place on or about January 21, 1882, at Green River (called Blake City in other reports), in Emery County, Utah, after Duffy shot and killed a fellow railroad worker, William Neugent, known as "California Bill." A number of men chased and captured Duffy, and he escaped lynching only through the intercession of others before being held in the Provo jail. None of the reports states the race of anyone involved.

Duffy and Neugent shared a bed as "bunkeys" and worked for Neilson & Jensen, railroad contractors east of Green River. According to an eyewitness, they quarreled on the way to camp, drank together, quarreled again, and parted. Other accounts said that Neugent had whipped Duffy in a fight earlier that day.

The two men met again in front of Taylor's saloon, Neugent with a pistol and Duffy with a rifle, and Neugent's shot passed through the calf of Duffy's left leg. Duffy's return shot struck Neugent in the left breast, and he fell back into the saloon and died almost at once.

Duffy then ran across the river, "followed by a number of men," who caught him after a short chase. The Herald's informant said it was "only through the intercession of the cooler headed men that he escaped being lynched," while the Evening News account said that "threats of lynching Duffy were freely indulged in."

By February 10 Duffy was in the Provo jail. No report of an inquest, indictment or trial appears in the coverage. The Evening News called the killing the second homicide in Emery County within a short time.

Brief items in the Butte Semi-Weekly Miner, headed "A Utah Murder," and the Elko Independent reported only the killing of "California Bill" at Blake City, without mention of a mob. The lynching threat appeared in the Utah-sourced accounts: a Salt Lake Evening News report, from D. K. Reid of Castle Dale, reprinted in the Dillon Tribune on February 4, and a letter from the Salt Lake Herald's Price River correspondent "Felix" on February 15. Felix credited the "cooler headed men" with saving Duffy but, in the next paragraph, wrote that the safety of "peaceable" citizens required that some local "roughs" be made to "dance on nothing."

The Butte brief dated the shooting Sunday, January 22, while the other three reports gave the 21st. The eyewitness placed the shooting at Green River, whereas the other reports named Blake City, and the coverage does not say whether the two names refer to the same place.

reader.title: Attempted lynching of William Duffy
chips: Lynching of any race (not in the anti-Black count)
bases: A group of men chased and captured Duffy after he shot a fellow railroad worker and he 'escaped being lynched' only through the intercession of others (A4), with 'threats of lynching' reported by a second source (A2); the race of those involved is not stated.
Duffy was captured by 'a number of men' who threatened to lynch him for the killing of Neugent, but he was not killed and was taken to the Provo jail (A4, A2); no one was killed by the group.

Two independent accounts, an eyewitness relayed by the Herald's correspondent (A4) and D. K. Reid's report to the Evening News (A2), agree that Duffy shot Neugent/Nugent and was threatened with lynching; wire briefs confirm the killing (A1, A3).

accounts.label: D. K. Reid via Evening News
accounts.gist: After getting the worst of a fight, Duffy procured a Winchester and shot Nugent; Nugent wounded him in the leg; threats of lynching Duffy were freely made.

accounts.label: Wire briefs
accounts.gist: Report only the killing of 'California Bill' by Duffy at Blake City, with no mention of a mob.
